# promptless — full architecture reference

## Classification pipeline (lib/classifier.sh)

The classifier resolves every terminal input into one of two paths:
native shell command, or natural-language prompt to opencode.

### Hot path: $PATH cache lookup

At shell startup, `build_command_cache()` populates an associative
array `COMMAND_CACHE` from `compgen -c`. Every input's first word is
looked up in this hash. If found *and* not on the ambiguous-verb list,
the input is a command — the check is O(1) and completes in under 10µs.

### Ambiguous verbs

`is_ambiguous_verb()` lists ~200 words that exist as both Unix commands
and English verbs ("find", "make", "test", "build", "delete", etc.).
These bypass the hot-path shortcut and fall through to further checks.

### Shell builtins

A `case` pattern matches bash builtins (cd, echo, export, source, alias,
eval, exec, exit, type, which, help, time, set, unset, shift, umask,
enable, bind, declare, typeset, local, readonly, printf, mapfile,
readarray, builtin, caller, command, compgen, complete, compopt, dirs,
disown, getopts, popd, pushd, pwd, return, shopt, suspend, trap, times,
false, ulimit, logout, continue, break). These always run as commands.

### Shell metacharacter detection

Inputs containing pipes (`|`), redirects (`>`, `<`), background (`&`),
command separators (`;`), backticks (`` ` ``), or flags (`--flag`) are
commands. Inputs starting with `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, `!`, or `#` are
commands. Single-word unknown inputs fall through to shell execution
(the safe default).

### NLP signal detection

Inputs ending with `?` or starting with interrogative words (how, what,
why, when, where, who, which, whose, can, could, would, should, is,
are, do, does, did, will, shall, may, might, please, tell, explain,
describe) are classified as prompts.

### NLP structure detection (has_nlp_structure)

The remainder text (everything after the first word) is padded with
spaces and matched against 70+ English function words using bash `case`
word-boundary patterns:

- Determiners: a, an, the, my, our, your, her, his, its, me, us, them, this, these, those, that, it
- Prepositions: to, for, of, in, on, at, from, about, with, without
- Conjunctions: and, or, but, if, not
- Modals: should, could, would, might, will, must, can, does
- Adverbs: just, also, only, very, really, please, maybe, perhaps, probably
- Copula: is, are, was, were, have, has, had, been, being, be, am
- Quantifiers: some, all, every, any
- Question words: what, where, when, why, how
- Similative: like

A match on the strong NLP signals (a, the, my, our, your) in the
padded arguments returns immediately as a prompt. Before doing so,
the function checks for file extensions (`*.py`, `*.json`, etc.)
in the arguments — if present, the input is more likely a command
with file arguments and returns as a command.

## opencode_with_context (lib/classifier.sh)

Launches opencode in JSON-streaming mode with `--auto` so tool calls
execute without interactive permission prompts. The stream is piped
through `format_output.py` for terminal rendering.

Session persistence:
1. `read_project_session()` reads `.promptless-session` from the
   current project root (found by `find_project_root()` walking up
   from $PWD looking for `.git`, `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `go.mod`,
   `composer.json`, or `Makefile`).
2. If a session ID exists, opencode is invoked with `--session <id>`
   to continue the existing conversation.
3. `format_output.py` captures the session ID from the first JSON
   event and writes it back to `.promptless-session`.

## format_output.py — event parser

Reads newline-delimited JSON from stdin and formats each event type:

- `step_start`: silently skipped
- `text`: `part.text` is unescaped and written to stdout in real-time
- `tool_use`:
  - completed: green checkmark, shell command shown, output printed
  - error: red cross, error message and attempted command shown
  - running: yellow spinner with command
- `step_finish`: dimmed token stats (input/output counts) on stderr
- Non-JSON lines (provider stderr): passed through verbatim

Session ID is captured from the first event's `sessionID` field and
written to the file path given as the first CLI argument.

ANSI colour codes are applied only when stdout is a TTY.

## Bash integration (shell/promptless.bash)

Enter (`\C-m`) is bound to `\C-x\C-p\n`:

- `bind -x '"\C-x\C-p": classify_and_route'`
- `bind '"\C-m": "\C-x\C-p\n"'`

`classify_and_route()` inspects `$READLINE_LINE`:
- Escape hatches: `/new` and `/reset` call `reset_project_session()`
- Commands: no-op, the trailing `\n` accepts the line for normal execution
- Prompts: rewrites `READLINE_LINE` to `opencode_with_context <escaped>`,
  sets `READLINE_POINT` to end, then `\n` accepts it

The history entry is added manually via `history -s` before rewriting
the line.

## Zsh integration (shell/promptless.zsh)

ZLE widget override:

- `zle -N promptless_accept_line` replaces `accept-line`
- `bindkey '^M' promptless_accept_line` and `bindkey '^J'` for Enter

`promptless_accept_line()` inspects `$BUFFER`:
- Escape hatches: `/new`/`/reset` reset session and show `zle -M` message
- Commands: delegates to `zle .accept-line`
- Prompts: `print -s "$user_input"` to history, clears `BUFFER`,
  `zle -I` releases terminal, then calls `opencode_with_context` directly

## Session management functions

- `find_project_root()`: walks up from $PWD looking for version-control
  or project markers. Falls back to current directory if none found.
- `project_session_file()`: returns `$PROJECT_ROOT/.promptless-session`
- `read_project_session()`: cats the session file if it exists
- `write_project_session()`: writes a session ID to the file
- `reset_project_session()`: deletes the session file

## Testing

`test/test_classifier.sh` runs 37 test cases:
- 7 known command assertions (ls, git, cd, echo, export, source, scripts)
- 20 natural-language prompt assertions (interrogative sentences, imperatives with function words)
- 10 edge cases (empty input, escaped commands, pipes, redirects, flags,
  single unknown words, bare nouns, "teach me" pattern)
